title: STAT120 - Statistical Computing in R
text:
Wide variety, very flexible - can generate quite complicated graphs

http://www.htmlwidgets.org/showcase_leaflet.html
https://plot.ly/r/

Many new packages and functions are being published (esp. on github)
Currently, no “go-to” package, no unified approach
We’ll try a few simple examples to give you an idea, mostly using the plotly package


#install.packages('plotly')
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2)
library(Lock5Data)

title: Yi Lu
text:
Hi! I am an Associate Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at Drew University in Madison, New Jersey. I teach courses in statistics and data science, and I enjoy working on fun, applied research projects with students and collaborators.
I earned a Ph.D. in Statistics from the Ohio State University. My research background is in functional data analysis, Bayesian models, and Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. I love simulation-based methods (since the alternative, analytical derivations, are often daunting to me). I am a big fan of R.
I love jogging and running in my spare time. I am always out on a run, and my statistics classes tend to have too many running examples. I want to run an ultra-marathon one day.
You can find my CV here.
You can email me at ylu1@drew.edu.
This website is built with Quarto and VS Code.
